- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.33) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a 1–3% downward correction in the following 5–7 days.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if price is trending sharply upward, forecast often peaks too early; adjust downward 1–2% in the 5–10 day horizon.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate in early horizon (days 1–7) when sentiment is volatile; apply 1–3% downward adjustment for days 1–7.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67), model often fails to adjust; apply a 1–2% correction in direction of sentiment shift.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often misses mean reversion; add 1–2% downward bias for 5–10 day horizon.
